newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends up on BPA cuts, gas prices.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends up on BPA cuts, gas prices.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended higher Thursday with front months surging to new levels as the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) said it would not be offering surplus power Friday, industry sources said.

The lack of spot Northwest supply, combined with strong San Juan natural gas prices and forecasts of below and much below temperatures in the West into early November boosted the futures contracts, the sources said.
Traders also noted the power futures contracts may have seen some strength ahead of Monday's expiry of the November front months.

November California Oregon Border (COB) finished 85 cents higher at $20.25 after hitting a new contract high of $20.65 per megawatt hour (MWh), while December climbed 42 cents to $20.65 after reaching as high as $20.80 per MWh.
Remaining COB deferreds were mostly steady to up to 54 cents higher.
November Palo Verde (PV) settled up 48 cents at $18.93 after hitting a new contract high of $19.45, while December closed up 25 cents at $18.80 after reaching a new high of $19.50.
January PV settled down 10 cents at $17.50 although it did trade up to a new high of $18.25 per MWh.
Remaining PV deferreds finished mostly 35 cents higher.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 313 COB and 235 PV contracts traded Thursday.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
